documents: Oda, Fujii, Takenaka (2022) Simultaneous Sampling of NO, NO2, HONO and HNO3 in the Atmosphere by a Filter-Pack Method, Asian Journal of Atmospheric Environment 16(2) 2022006 (published PDF, 8 pages)

entry.evidence: Therefore, it is very difficult to obtain concentrations of NO and NO2.

steps.action: Reviewed existing NO2 and NO sampling methods (Saltzman, Jacobs-Hochheiser, annular denuders, TEA, NaI-Na2CO3 and PTIO filter packs) and their limitations as motivation.
steps.quote: Toriyama et al. (2019) measured HNO3, HONO and NO2 simultaneously with filter-pack sampling.

steps.action: Took guaiacol as the NO2 absorbent from a published denuder study reporting high absorption at high flow rates.
steps.quote: Buttini et al. (1987) applied guaiacol as an absorbent for NO2 in a denuder system.

steps.action: Built a two-filter-pack sampler (FP1: Teflon, NaCl and Na2CO3 filters; FP2: guaiacol filters, KMnO4 oxidation filter, guaiacol filters) and defined equations (1)-(4) for each species from nitrite and nitrate.
steps.quote: The sampling system consists of two filter-pack sets

steps.action: Adopted FP1 sampling conditions and HNO3/HONO collection efficiencies from the authors' earlier study.
steps.quote: The sampling condition of FP1 was according to that of Toriyama et al. (2019).

steps.action: Compared NO2 collected on filters impregnated with 10, 15 and 20 wt% guaiacol against the chemiluminescence analyzer.
steps.quote: At 15 wt%, the NO2 concentrations measured by the present method were in good agreement with those measured by the CL method.

steps.action: Rejected 10 wt% (incomplete absorption) and 20 wt% (large scatter) and fixed guaiacol at 15 wt%.
steps.quote: At 10wt% guaiacol, NO2 was not completely absorbed on the filter.

steps.action: Measured NO2 collection efficiency with two filters in series at flow rates 0.1-0.5 dm3 min-1 on outdoor air.
steps.quote: almost all NO2 could be collected

steps.action: Set the FP2 flow rate at 0.3 dm3 min-1 as a safety margin and checked its balance with the FP1 flow for HONO.
steps.quote: we decided that 0.3 dm3 min-1 was to be used in the sampling for safety

steps.action: Chose KMnO4 as the NO oxidant over chromium oxide, PTIO and ozone on practical grounds.
steps.quote: Therefore, in this study, KMnO4 was used to oxidize NO.

steps.action: Measured NO oxidation efficiency for KMnO4 concentrations 0.02-0.2 mol dm-3 at 80 ppb NO and at 320 ppb, finding nearly 100% against 70% in the JIS method.
steps.quote: The oxidation efficiencies were higher than 80% from 0.02-0.2 mol dm-3 KMnO4 and stable at 0.16 mol dm-3 KMnO4.

steps.action: Estimated the oxidation capacity of the KMnO4 filter from a 2.75 h, 300 ppb test and extrapolated it to 183 h at 60 ppb and 0.3 dm3 min-1.
steps.quote: a total of 8.24×10-6 mol of NO could be oxidized continuously

steps.action: Under the optimum conditions, compared ambient NO and NO2 (summed with HNO3 and HONO) from the filter pack against chemiluminescence on several dates.
steps.quote: Both lines showed a good linear relationship with a slope of almost 1.0

steps.action: Calculated detection limits for HNO3, HONO, NO2 and NO for 4 h sampling from ion measurement errors and blank filters.
steps.quote: The detection limits of these gases depend on the sampling time.

steps.action: Deployed three sampler sets simultaneously at an urban, a heavy-traffic roadside and a suburban site around Osaka in morning and afternoon periods.
steps.quote: Three sets of the present system were applied for simultaneous measurements of HNO3, HONO, NO2 and NO.

steps.action: Reported the four species' concentrations at the three sites.
steps.quote: For NO2, the highest concentration, 83.8 ppb, was observed in the afternoon at IZM.

steps.action: Related the between-site differences in NO and NO2 to traffic volume, including traffic counts at IZM.
steps.quote: The NO2 concentration at SAN was lower than that at the other two points. This was due to the lower traffic at SAN.

steps.action: Flagged the IZM morning NO value as underestimated because the KMnO4 filter decolorized, and attributed this to vehicle-emitted reductants rather than to the method.
steps.quote: the NO concentration in the morning at IZM must have been undercalculated.

steps.action: Changed the KMnO4 filter every two hours in the afternoon and recommended several oxidation filters in series at highly polluted sites.
steps.quote: several KMnO4 filters should be connected in series

steps.action: Concluded that the simultaneous filter-pack sampling method is established and suggested battery operation for sites without power.
steps.quote: [...] simultaneous sampling method for NO, NO2, HONO and HNO3 by using a filter-pack was established.

tree.answer: No natural phenomenon is posed; the need is low-cost NOx measurement where monitors are lacking
Gases are collected on filters and measured indirectly as nitrite and nitrate
Develop and characterize a simultaneous filter-pack sampler for NO, NO2, HONO and HNO3
No rival hypotheses; alternative absorbents and oxidants are considered as design choices
Parameters are set in tests with standard gases and ambient air; field conditions are found at three sites
Agreement with chemiluminescence holds across guaiacol and KMnO4 levels, flow rates and dates; KMnO4 capacity failed at IZM in the morning
Method kept as established, with a recommendation for multiple oxidation filters

end.claim: A filter-pack method using guaiacol (15 wt%) and KMnO4 (0.16 mol dm-3) filters at 0.3 dm3 min-1 simultaneously samples NO, NO2, HONO and HNO3, agreeing with chemiluminescence (slopes 0.987 and 1.04), with an estimated 183 h oxidation capacity at 60 ppb NO.

decisive_move.sentence: The ambient comparison of filter-pack NO and NO2 against the chemiluminescence analyzer under the optimum conditions is the evidence that the method measures what it claims.

gates.evidence: No hypothesis directed the data acquisition; parameters were chosen by trial against a reference. The method could have disagreed with chemiluminescence, and it did fail in part at IZM, where the KMnO4 filter was exhausted. No analysis or acceptance threshold is stated as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Griess-Ilosvay colorimetric nitrite determination with UV/Vis spectrophotometry
Anion ion chromatography for nitrite and nitrate
Conversion of NO2 to nitrite in alkaline guaiacol solution (Nash 1970)
KMnO4 oxidation of NO from the Japanese Industrial Standard and Saltzman method

novelty_claims.quote: This method can measure NO2 at shorter sampling times than the previously reported method (Toriyama et al., 2019).

limits: Internal inconsistencies: Fig. 2 caption gives a flow of 1.0 dm3 min-1, while the text gives 0.1; the text gives the field date as September 15, 2020, while Table 1 says September 17; the NO correlation coefficient is 0.998 in the text and 0.995 in Fig. 5. The chemiluminescence reference for NO2 includes other nitrogen compounds, and organics are neglected without a test. No uncertainties on the slopes and no sample counts per comparison are reported beyond the figures. The 183 h capacity is a linear extrapolation from one 2.75 h test, not a measured endurance. Interferences (O3, PAN, HONO on guaiacol) are not tested here. The HNO3 particle-evaporation artifact is argued away by low concentrations, not checked. HONO and HNO3 collection efficiencies are inherited from Toriyama et al. (2019). The reductant explanation for KMnO4 exhaustion at IZM is speculation. The attribution of site differences to traffic is a sub-claim at best_explanation, based on one day of sampling. The higher-than-JIS oxidation efficiency is explained only by speculation. Coding choice: composition capability_first fits loosely; no phenomenon or question follows the capability beyond a demonstration field application (inference).

disagreements.target: Toriyama et al. (2019) TEA filter-pack NO2 sampling
disagreements.support: Their TEA filter needs 0.1 dm3 min-1 for complete absorption; the guaiacol filter here collects nearly all NO2 below 0.4 dm3 min-1.
disagreements.quote: [...] is not suitable to measure NO2 in a few hours.

disagreements.target: Japanese Industrial Standard (2004) KMnO4 oxidation efficiency of 70%
disagreements.support: The KMnO4-impregnated filter gave nearly 100% oxidation, attributed speculatively to better contact on a wet solid than in aqueous solution.
disagreements.quote: [...] of NO to NO2 at 70% is used in the Japanese Industrial Standard (2004), but almost 100% was obtained in our results.

disagreements.target: Saltzman and Jacobs-Hochheiser modifications of the Griess-Ilosvay method
disagreements.support: Cites Tamaki and Hiraki (1988) on uncertainties in conversion, absorption and oxidation efficiencies.
disagreements.quote: however, there are uncertainties in this method

disagreements.target: Annular denuder systems (Allegrini et al., 1987; Ferm and Sjodin, 1985)
disagreements.support: Practical argument only: cost, fragility and complex operation.
disagreements.quote: The annular denuder system is expensive and easily broken because of glassware, and the operation is complicated.

alternatives_considered.reason: denuder expensive, easily broken, complicated operation
guaiacol absorbs enough NO2 at high flow (Buttini et al.); TEA requires low flow
chromium socially problematic in Japan; PTIO needs extra separation; ozone needs a UV lamp and power
10 wt% incomplete absorption; 20 wt% large scatter
near-complete collection below 0.4; 0.3 chosen for safety
efficiency stable at 0.16; same as the Saltzman/JIS oxidant concentration

alternatives_considered.chosen: analyse only nitrite on guaiacol filters
alternatives_considered.reason: only nitrite seen in earlier experiment; Nash (1970)

alternatives_considered.chosen: ignore nitrogen-containing organics in the CL comparison
